The gate asserts nothing about the draft field (`interaction-check.mjs` mentions undo only in a comment), so this is not a restatement. Severity is blocking on the stated definition: the product speaks an instruction into the live region and prints it on the strip, and the key is dead at the one focus location the product itself chose.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED.

1. The code contradicts its own prose, destructively. The note says "A draft with typed text keeps native text undo." The snippet does the opposite: `event.preventDefault()` is unconditional and `undoLast()` is unconditional — only `discardDraft()` sits behind the `!draftText.trim()` guard. So a person mid-sentence in the composer who presses Ctrl+Z to take back a typo gets no character back (native undo is preventDefault'd away) and instead has the previously committed card silently spliced off the board, with "… removed again." spoken over them. I measured today's behaviour for that exact case: type "Chase the florist" into the fresh draft, Ctrl+Z → the field returns to empty, the board is untouched, nothing is announced. The fix replaces a harmless browser-owned undo with undo destroying a committed task while somebody is typing — the failure Notes wrote a five-line comment about and guarded against. That alone is fatal.

2. It regresses the empty-history case. Empty draft, nothing on `undoHistory`: the fix calls `discardDraft()` (which closes the composer, says "Discarded.", mounts and runs `leaveDraft()` to `.trayAdd`) and then `undoLast()` says "Nothing left to undo." So a keystroke that undoes nothing tears down the open composer and moves focus out of it. Ctrl+Z must never be the key that closes your composer.

Two `say()` calls and two `mount()`s for one keystroke. `discardDraft()` speaks "Discarded." into the same polite `.sr` node that `runUndo` then overwrites with "… removed again." in the same tick, so the first sentence is clobbered before any AT reads it — and "Discarded." is the wrong receipt anyway, since the branch is defined by the draft being empty and the same word is Escape's receipt for deliberately abandoning typed words.

standing.fix: In the same post-layout pass that sets `--body-bottom`, for each overflowing `.trayBody` compute the offset of the last card that fits entirely — `[...body.querySelectorAll('.card')].filter(c => c.offsetTop + c.offsetHeight <= body.clientHeight).pop()` — and set `body.style.blockSize` to that card's bottom offset (clearing the inline size when the body no longer overflows). The scroller then always ends in the 8px gutter between cards, the existing hairline lands in that gutter, and the leftover pixels fall to the tray's bottom padding above the Add row. No new colour, no mask, no change to the snap model.
standing.assertion: For `tasks.board` and `tasks.dense` at 390x844, 768x1024, 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, walk every text node inside every `.trayBody` and assert that no client rect straddles the scroller's bottom edge (never `rect.top < body.bottom - 0.5 && rect.bottom > body.bottom + 0.5`); and assert that every partially-visible `.card` shows either 0px or its full height.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE OBSERVATION — and the fix is not merely wrong, it makes every number in the finding worse. Do not discard the observation; do not ship this remedy.

THE OBSERVATION REPRODUCES, ALMOST EXACTLY. Chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.dense`, Range/getClientRects sweep against each `.trayBody`'s bottom edge at rest. 1920x1000: To do cuts "Enquiry" 7.5 into a 14px line, In progress cuts "Aisling & Tom" 8.9 into 16px, Done cuts "Deposit invoice settled, Mara & Finn" 13.2 into 18px — all three verbatim. 1440x960: three lanes, "Nora & Cian deposit received" showing 3.1 of 18 — verbatim. 1280x900: three lanes. 1120x820: Done is a 5.5px sliver of a 98px card — verbatim. tasks.board clean at 1280/1440/1920, cuts at 768 (Done, "Mara & Finn", 6.4 of 16 — verbatim) and 390 (two lanes). Only one number is off: dense at 390 cuts two lanes, not three (Done there is a 10.9px sliver carrying no line box). The mechanism is stated correctly too — snap governs rest-after-scroll, nothing governs the start.

THE FIX IS ARITHMETICALLY WRONG BECAUSE IT MEASURES IN THE WRONG COORDINATE SPACE. `.trayBody` declares no `position`; `.tray` declares `position: relative` (line 1279). I confirmed at runtime that every card's `offsetParent` is `.tray`, not `.trayBody` — card `offsetTop` values in To do at 1920 are 66, 210, 316, 459…, where 66 is the head's own height. So `c.offsetTop + c.offsetHeight <= body.clientHeight` compares tray-relative tops against the body's height, and `body.style.blockSize = <that card's bottom offset>` assigns a tray-relative number as a block-size. The file's own `measureEdges` gets this right two lines away — `last.offsetTop - body.offsetTop + last.offsetHeight` — and the fix drops the `- body.offsetTop`.

I RAN THE FIX AS WRITTEN. 1920x1000, tasks.dense, three consecutive passes:
1. It does not fix the cut — it doubles it. Before: three of five lanes cut type. After: FIVE of five, each ~9-10px into a 21px line ("Enquiry." 9.3/21, "Aisling & Tom." 9.7/21, "Bar. High priority." 9.4/21, "Held 21 days, since 25 Jun" 10/21, "Nora & Cian" 9/16), each ending ~55px into a card. The 66px error lands the new edge mid-card every time.
2. It breaks two lanes that were clean. Waiting and Under review do not overflow at 1920 (`data-more` absent, all content visible, no cut). The filter still returns a "last fitting card" there and clamps them: review 464→413, waiting 233→183. Content that was fully on screen is now hidden and cut mid-line. The finding's guard — "clearing the inline size when the body no longer overflows" — never fires, because the clamp is what creates the overflow. Passes 2 and 3 confirm it latches.
3. Its claim about where the leftover pixels go is false about the code, and this is the seat's own subject. `.tray` is `padding: 14px 12px 0` — no bottom padding — and `.trayAdd` is `flex: none; margin-top: 4px` with no auto margin. Today all five "Add here" rows sit flush at the tray foot (top 862, tray bottom 898 at 1920). After the fix: 843, 843, 612, 382, 787 — five Add rows at five heights, up to 461px apart, each floating over 55-516px of empty white above an unchanged tray foot. The shared `.tray::after` hairline, which is drawn at `--body-bottom`, goes ragged with them. A UI-composition finding that trades one straight rule across the board for five staggered rules and five staggered Add rows is a net loss.

SEVERITY. The seat declares none; the class is defect, not more, which is exactly where `dense-board-cuts-a-word-in-half` (r3) left it. A scroll container clipping its content is the universal behaviour of every list in Linear, Stripe and Vercel, and the partial card is itself the overflow cue the hairline seconds. This is the third filing of this surface (`tray-clips-cards-mid-line` r1, `dense-board-cuts-a-word-in-half` r3); filing it again with a new remedy was legitimate, and the remedy is worse than the disease.
standing.breaks:
The fix as filed breaks three things I measured: it cuts type in five lanes instead of three; it clamps and clips two lanes (Waiting, Under review at 1920) that do not overflow at all, hiding visible content; and it lifts the five "Add here" rows to five different heights (843/843/612/382/787 against an unchanged tray foot at 898), taking the `.tray::after` hairline ragged with them. It also latches — `measureEdges` runs on every scroll (13283) and every repaint (13137), the clamp keeps the body overflowing, so the "clear when it no longer overflows" release never fires.

If the sharpened version lands, re-measure: (a) the Range sweep at 390/768/1120/1280/1440/1920 across `tasks.dense`, `tasks.board` and the filtered board — zero cut line boxes is the pass, and any lane whose `data-more` state flips is a regression; (b) the five `.trayAdd` rect tops per viewport — they must stay equal in overflowing lanes and equal to trayBottom − 36; (c) the spread of `--body-bottom` across the five trays, which is the new composition cost and the reason to reconsider shipping it; (d) three consecutive `measureEdges` passes at one viewport, asserting `clientHeight` is identical on passes 2 and 3, since the ratchet is the failure mode; (e) the compact-density and stacked-header paths, where the head is a different height and the dropped `- body.offsetTop` term would have had a different magnitude; (f) keyboard carry and the completion FLIP, which scroll the body and re-enter `measureEdges` mid-animation — the existing comment at `extent` warns that `scrollHeight` lies during the settle, and a height clamp that fires there will pump the layout; (g) `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs`, both currently green.

standing.element: [data-app="notes"] .desk / .deskAside / .index — Notes, reading a note
standing.problem: The desk's height is set entirely by the metadata rail, not by the note. `.readBody` renders at a fixed 496px measure and 55–83px tall for every one of the 14 fixture notes (scrollHeight == clientHeight throughout; the 425px max-height is never reached), while `.deskAside` renders at 155, 224 or 275px depending on how many labelled facts that note carries. So `.desk` takes exactly three heights — 291, 360 and 411px — and the index below it takes exactly three tops — 426, 495 and 546px — identical at 1280, 1440 and 1920. Driven by clicking rows in order, the row you just clicked moves under your own pointer: row2 +99px, row3 +69px, row4 −158px, row9 −200px, row10 −122px. Nothing scrolls to compensate (index scrollTop stays 0); focus is correctly moved to `.readBody`, so the keyboard survives and the eye does not.
standing.consequence: Reading down her notebook is the thing Orla does most, and every note she opens throws the rest of the list up or down by as much as 200px. The next note she meant to read is no longer where she left it, so a second click lands on a different note than the one she was looking at. The list under her hand is not stable, and it is unstable for a reason she can never see: the length of the machine's metadata column.
standing.fix: Reserve the reading desk at one height. Give `.deskAside` a `min-block-size` equal to its tallest configuration (275px at desk widths, measured), so `.desk` renders 411px for every note and `.index` keeps one top. The already-empty lower half of the note column absorbs the reserve — it is the writing area "Write on it" opens into, so the space is not wasted. Leave the ≤720 branch alone, where the desk is `display: none`.
standing.assertion: At 1280x900, 1440x960 and 1920x1000, lift each of the 14 `.idxItem` rows in turn and assert `.desk` height is identical for all 14 (±1px) and `.index` top is identical for all 14 (±1px); and assert that clicking any `.idxItem` moves that element's own bounding-box top by 0px (±1px).
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, AND ON ONE LOAD-BEARING HALF OF THE OBSERVATION. Do not discard the geometry — the core measurement reproduces exactly — but do not ship this remedy.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, clicking each of the 14 index rows at 1280x900, 1440x960, 1920x1000): `.deskAside` renders at exactly 155 / 224 / 275px on a 3 / 4 / 5-fact note; `.desk` at exactly 291 / 360 / 411px; `.index` top at exactly 426 / 495 / 546px — identical at all three widths. `.readBody` is 496px wide and 55 or 83px tall for every fixture note, scrollHeight == clientHeight throughout, and its computed max-height is 365px at 1280, 425px at 1440, 465px at 1920 (the seat quoted the 1440 value as if it were the constant — minor, but it is one of three). Focus does land on `.readBody`. So the diagnosis "the desk's height is set by the metadata rail" is correct.

WHAT DOES NOT. "Nothing scrolls to compensate (index scrollTop stays 0)" is false, and it is the sentence the severity rests on. Driven clean at 1440x960 — click rows 0..13 in order, no synthetic scrolling — `.index` scrollTop goes 0, 0, 0, 0, 158, 158, 158, 187, 318, 319, 432, 432, 432, 502. The index scrolls the cursor row toward the top of its own viewport on click (it carries `scroll-padding-top: 66px` and `scroll-padding-bottom: var(--walk-reserve, 160px)`), so a large share of the displacement the seat attributes to the desk resize is in fact a deliberate scroll-into-view of the row you clicked. And the five quoted displacements do not reproduce under the seat's own stated protocol: I measured, in click order, +220, 0, −121, +69, −158, 0, 0, −29, −131, +50, −234, 0, +69, −70. Neither 0- nor 1-indexing maps "row2 +99 / row9 −200 / row10 −122" onto that. The phenomenon is real; the evidence offered for it is not the evidence that was measured.

THE FIX IS WRONG ON ITS NUMBER, ITS BOUNDARY, AND ITS JUSTIFICATION.

1. 275px is not the tallest configuration "at desk widths". The two-column desk starts at 1081px, not 1280. Measured on the 5-fact note: 1081 → aside 294px, desk 430, index top 565; 1100 → 294 / 430 / 565; 1160 and up → 275 / 411 / 546. Between 1081 and ~1150 the margin column is narrow enough that a fact wraps. A 275px `min-block-size` therefore leaves the desk taking TWO heights (411 and 430) across that band and the index still moving 19px — the finding does not fix its own problem where its own layout branch begins.

2. The named exemption is at the wrong breakpoint. The finding says "leave the ≤720 branch alone, where the desk is `display: none`". But the branch that matters is `@media (max-width: 1080px)`, where `.deskAside` becomes `grid-auto-flow: column` — a horizontal strip under the writing. Measured on the 5-fact note: 768 → aside 73px, desk 320; 900 → 73 / 320; 1024 → 73 / 328; 1080 → 73 / 328. An unqualified `min-block-size: 275px` injects 202px of dead white into the desk across the entire 721–1080 tablet band and pushes the index down by that much — on the widths where the index is already the more cramped of the two locked planes. As written, the fix ships that regression.

3. The justification is factually false. "The already-empty lower half of the note column absorbs the reserve — it is the writing area 'Write on it' opens into." It is not. Driven at 1440 on note 0: read mode desk 411, index top 546; press `[data-act="edit"]` and the desk becomes 347 with the index top at 482 — the textarea renders 116px and the foot moves out of the spanning row, so "Write on it" SHRINKS the desk by 64px. The aside is 275px in both states, so pinning the aside does not stabilise the desk across the note's own states either: after the fix the index would still jump 64px the moment you write on a note, and the reserved band would still be dead white in read mode, which is exactly the `notes-desk-half-empty` class this programme already adjudicated once.

SEVERITY. The seat implies more than this is worth. The product does nothing it does not say and asserts nothing untrue; the index does scroll the clicked row into view, and the row you clicked stays on screen in all 14 cases (`visBefore` true throughout). This is a defect — visibly wrong, passable — not blocking or misleading.
standing.sharpenedFix: Reserve, but scope it and use the measured number. (a) Put the reserve inside the two-column branch only — `@media (min-width: 1081px) { [data-app="notes"] .top[data-two] > .deskAside { min-block-size: 294px; } }` — so the 721–1080 band, where the aside is a 73px horizontal strip, is untouched. 294px is the measured tallest configuration (5 facts at 1081–1150, where the margin column wraps); 275px is only the tallest at ≥1160 and leaves the desk taking two heights below that. With 294 the desk renders 430px and `.index` keeps one top at 565px for every fixture note at every width ≥1081. (b) Either accept that "Write on it" still shortens the desk by 64px, or close that separately by keeping `.topFoot` spanning `1 / -1` in the edit template as it is in read, which is where the 64px goes. (c) If the dead band reads as empty rather than as desk, prefer holding the height on `.desk` rather than on the aside — the paper then stays honest to its content and the reserve is ground, not white paper — but re-check that the paper's own moving bottom edge is the lesser evil before choosing it.
standing.breaks:
The fix AS WRITTEN breaks the 721–1080 band: `.deskAside` there is a 73px horizontal strip, so a 275px floor adds 202px of dead paper and drives `.index` down from a 320–328px desk to ~522px, on the widths where the index has least room. It also fails to stabilise 1081–1160 (aside 294 > 275, two desk heights remain) and does nothing about the 64px the desk loses when the edit template renders.

AFTER THE SHARPENED FIX LANDS, RE-MEASURE: (1) `.readBody`'s height sum — it computes `max(120px, 100vh - var(--desk-chrome,311px) - var(--index-floor,224px) - var(--peel-h,0px))`, and `--desk-chrome: 311px` is commented as "measured at 1280, its widest". A permanent 294px aside makes the desk taller than that constant assumes, so re-derive 311 and re-check the note window at 1280x800 and 1440x900, not just at 1000px tall. (2) The index floor: confirm at least the five rows `--index-floor` is written to buy still render at 1281x800 with the taller desk. (3) The seam: `notes.seam` at 1440 measures aside 155 / desk 475 with the peel panel under the paper; a 294px floor pushes that desk to ~514, so re-check that `--peel-h` yielding still leaves the index reachable at 1280x800. (4) The three shipped 1920 frames (`shots/paper-notes.notebook`, `paper-notes.seam`) move — regenerate. (5) Re-run both gates: `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs` (the audit's hit-target and index-row rows sit below the desk and will shift).
